newsitem.title: NEPAL: Two U.S. climbers die in Nepal avalanche-embassy.
newsitem.headline: Two U.S. climbers die in Nepal avalanche-embassy.

text.p: Two American climbers were killed while attempting to scale Mount Annapurna IV peak in the Himalayan kingdom of Nepal, a U.S. embassy official said on Sunday.
The official said the climbers were identified as Debbie Marshall, 32, a forester from Glenwood Springs, Colorado, and Richard Davidson, 46, a computer engineer from New Mexico.

A Nepal's tourism ministry official said the two victims and a third climber, Dr Cleve Armstrong, were reported missing on Friday after an avalanche hit them at a height of 4,900 metres (16,072 feet) while they were climbing the 7,525-metre (24,682 foot) peak.
A Royal Nepal Army helicopter rescued Armstrong, 52, on Sunday morning and evacuated him to Nepal's capital Kathmandu.
Armstrong, a doctor from Denver, was leading a seven-member expedition.
"As a doctor himself, he (Armstrong) was able to confirm that the other two were dead," the embassy official said.
